paragraphs: Children in care across the North West are looked after by the region's councils, which now recruit together through two regional hubs funded by the Department for Education, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. When the northern hub launched in July 2024, the councils behind it said the North West alone needed 760 more foster carers.

That hub, Foster With Us, brings together Blackburn with Darwen, Blackpool, Cumberland, Westmorland and Furness, and Lancashire County Council, and was set up with £1.2 million from a regional pathfinder bid. At launch the five councils had 152 children aged from birth to 18 waiting for a foster home, 19 of them in sibling groups, and Cumberland said more than 700 children across Cumbria were in council care. The hub offers fostering advisors seven days a week, help through each stage of the application, a buddy scheme, free training and the Mockingbird model, in which several fostering families are supported by one experienced hub home.

Further south, eight councils in Cheshire and Merseyside launched Foster4 in May 2024. They said they had more than 4,600 children in care between them but only just over 1,150 approved council foster carers. Foster4 offers a single first point of contact, help with the application and a buddy who is already fostering locally.

Whichever part of the North West you live in, look at the page for your own town or county too. Speak to your council's hub and to two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about the children they most need homes for, their training and support, and what they pay.
